title: Salento, Maratea & the Amalfi Coast — June 2027

itinerary.labelHtml:
The Itinerary

Day by day

Swipe each carousel for photos. Every stop carries its cost, a 💰 money-saving tip, an ✨ splurge, picky-kid restaurants, backup / if-time ideas, blog links, and a map — tap “Open in Google Maps” to navigate. Each day also shows an estimated per-day cost — food + activities only (excludes lodging, flights, and the rental car).

days.heading: Depart Pittsburgh after work
days.note: No PTO needed for an evening departure after a full workday.

days.heading: Arrive Brindisi, drive to Gallipoli
days.note: Pick up the rental car at the airport, not a city branch — better automatic-transmission odds. Keep tonight light: check in, a short old-town walk, an early dinner.

days.heading: Gallipoli & Punta Prosciutto beach day

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Baia Verde or Spiaggia della Purità

days.note: Two beach personalities in one day — Gallipoli's town beach in the morning, the marine-reserve turquoise water at Punta Prosciutto in the afternoon.

spots.name: Gallipoli
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · GallipoliFlickr
spots.cost: Beach clubs on Baia Verde run €20-40/day for umbrella + 2 sunbeds (peaks near €40 in August); the free public beach in the old town costs nothing.
spots.climate: Air 75°F day / 61°F night. Sea warms from ~70°F early June to ~73°F by month's end — comfortable, not warm yet.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the paid lidos for Spiaggia della Purità, the free public beach tucked below the old town's walls — no rental fee, no parking cost.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Half-day boat trip to the sea caves and coves near Punta Pizzo/Santa Maria di Leuca, ~€30-45/person, with swim stops unreachable on foot.
spots.restoHtml:
• Osteria Briganti — seafood osteria in the old town alleys, fresh catch and pasta
  • La Vinaigrette — seafront on the old town's Riviera, Salento seasonal dishes
  • La Pizza da Franco — wood-fired pizzeria, straightforward margherita for picky eaters
spots.altboxHtml:
• Punta della Suina ↩ — pine-forest beach 4km south, nicknamed the "Caribbean of the Ionian," quieter than Baia Verde with both free and lido sections.
  • Torre Lapillo ↗ — same clear water as Punta Prosciutto with more restaurants and services nearby.
  • Nardo old town ↗ — authentic baroque lanes with fewer day-trippers than the headline towns.

spots.name: Punta Prosciutto & Porto Cesareo
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Punta ProsciuttoIG · Porto CesareoFlickr
spots.cost: Lido sunbed + umbrella ~€15-20/day in June (rising to €40-50 in peak Jul/Aug); long free public stretches exist, e.g. near Riva degli Angeli.
spots.climate: Air 78°F day / 70°F night. Sea ~72°F — the shallow, gently-sloping sandbar warms faster than deeper coves.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the free beach stretch south of the equipped lidos near Riva degli Angeli — same white sand and turquoise water, no rental fee.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Samanà Beach, a beach club inside the marine reserve known for exceptionally clear water — front-row sunbeds ~€30-70/day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Fisheria — panoramic seafront terrace, fresh raw seafood and fish sandwiches
  • Grecale — waterfront over the small port, Gallipoli shrimp and catch of the day
  • Il Graffio — steps from the beach, serves pizza alongside seafood — reliable picky-kid fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Torre Lapillo ↩ — the beach immediately between Porto Cesareo and Punta Prosciutto — same fine sand and clear water, with more restaurants and services nearby.
  • Nardo old town ↗ — authentic baroque lanes with fewer day-trippers than the headline towns.
  • Torre dell Orso ↗ — gold-sand bay north of Otranto with the Due Sorelle sea stacks offshore.

days.heading: Relaxed Salento beach day

facts.label: Focus
facts.valueHtml: Pescoluse shallows, beach lunch, optional Nardò stroll

days.note: Last two Salento days deliberately stay low-key before the long transfer.

spots.name: Pescoluse (Le Maldive del Salento)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · PescoluseFlickr
spots.cost: Beach access is free; budget ~€20-40 for a lido umbrella/loungers if you want shade and bathrooms, plus a casual lunch. Parking is usually the only unavoidable extra.
spots.climate: Air ~80°F day / ~68°F night. Sea ~72°F — shallow sand and clear water make this one of the easiest kid swims in Salento.
spots.saveHtml: Save Bring towels and use the free beach, then keep lunch simple with focaccia, fruit, and cold drinks from town.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a front-row umbrella at a lido so the day has shade, bathrooms, and no logistics beyond swimming and lunch.
spots.restoHtml:
• Maldive del Salento lido — beach bar/restaurant setup right on the sand when you want the easiest family lunch
  • Ikarus — restaurant-pizzeria about 50m from the beach, useful for plain pasta or pizza
  • Boteguita Beach Pub — casual beach food, snacks, and cold drinks close to the water
spots.altboxHtml:
• Nardò ↩ — about 25 minutes from Gallipoli, an authentic baroque old town with real local life and far fewer day-trippers.
  • Nardo old town ↗ — authentic baroque lanes with fewer day-trippers than the headline towns.
  • Torre dell Orso ↗ — gold-sand bay north of Otranto with the Due Sorelle sea stacks offshore.

days.heading: Otranto day trip

facts.label: Focus
facts.valueHtml: Castello Aragonese, the cathedral mosaic, Baia dei Turchi

days.note: Last full Salento day — pack the old town and a swim into one trip before tomorrow's long drive.

spots.name: Otranto
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · OtrantoFlickr
spots.cost: Castello Aragonese: €3 adult / €2 ages 6-14. Cathedral (mosaic floor) is free. Lido sunbeds ~€20-30/day for two; free rocky bathing spots exist south of the old town.
spots.climate: Sea ~68°F — start of comfortable swimming season. Air estimated ~78°F day / ~66°F night (regional figure, not independently confirmed for Otranto specifically).
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk 10-15 minutes south along the seafront to Spiaggia dei Gradoni (Baia del Turco), a free rocky bathing spot with ladders into clear water.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Half-day boat excursion from the harbor up the coast to Baia dei Turchi and the sea caves of the Riviera degli Haethey, ~€35-85/person.
spots.restoHtml:
• Trattoria Da Sergio — family-run seafood trattoria near the cathedral, linguine with two shrimp
  • Acmet Pascià — harbor-view seafood restaurant in the town center
  • Lu Tata N'zinu — busy, well-reviewed pizzeria — thin crispy pizza and fries, expect a wait
spots.altboxHtml:
• Torre dell'Orso ↩ — a golden-sand bay 20 minutes north framed by pine forest, famous for the "Due Sorelle" sea stacks just offshore.
  • Porto Selvaggio ↗ — pine-forest coastal reserve if the family wants nature over a lido.
  • Punta della Suina ↗ — pine-backed Ionian beach south of Gallipoli with a prettier, quieter feel.

days.heading: Transfer: Gallipoli → Maratea

facts.label: Route
facts.valueHtml: Inland via the A2 — avoid the coastal SS106

days.note: The longest drive of the trip. Route inland rather than trusting GPS onto the Calabria coastal road, and plan a real rest stop partway.

days.heading: Maratea town & the Christ statue

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Cristo Redentore overlook via the summer shuttle

days.note: Go early if you want to skip the shuttle line and drive up yourself before the summer car ban kicks in.

spots.name: Maratea Town & Cristo Redentore
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · MarateaIG · Cristo RedentoreFlickr
spots.cost: Viewing the Christ statue is free; summer shuttle from the parking lot up to the basilica runs ~€1-2/person plus ~€2-5 parking (estimated, ballpark).
spots.climate: Air ~74°F day / ~68°F night, can spike to 93°F. Sea ~72°F (interpolated from May/August readings, not a direct June figure).
spots.saveHtml: Save Arrive before 9am or visit off-peak hours when the summit road is open to cars — skips the ~€2/person shuttle and parking fee entirely.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private 2-hour guided walking tour of the historic Borgo, Basilica, and statue area — around $336 for the whole group, not per person.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria La Bussola — wood-fired neighborhood pizzeria, pizzas from ~€8, margherita for kids
  • Za' Mariuccia — harborfront terrace since 1958, seafood — ask for plain pasta for kids
  • Taverna Rovita — Michelin-listed old-town kitchen since 1981 — treat as the parents' night out, ask ahead for a plain pasta
spots.altboxHtml:
• Diamante, Calabria ↩ — "the town of murals," ~45 min south — a livelier, flatter promenade town if the steep old-town lanes feel like too much with a tired 8-year-old.
  • Arcomagno cove ↗ — natural sea-arch cove south of Maratea; sandier and no boat required.
  • Fiumicello Beach ↗ — easier Maratea beach day with services when sea-cave logistics feel heavy.

days.heading: Maratea beaches & sea caves

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Cala Jannita or the harbor coves

days.note: A completely different coastline from Salento — rockier, cooler water, dramatic cliffs instead of flat sand.

spots.name: Maratea Beaches & Sea Caves
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · MarateaFlickr
spots.cost: Grotta delle Meraviglie (walk-in show cave): €5/adult, free under 6. Private half-day boat charter for grottoes/swim stops: from €120 for the whole boat.
spots.climate: Air ~74°F day. Sea ~72°F — same interpolated estimate as Maratea town, this is one small coastline.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk into the Grotta delle Meraviglie (€5/person) instead of a paid boat tour — a family of 4 sees a real sea cave for ~€15-20 total.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Private half-day boat charter along the coast (Freedome or similar) — from €120 for the boat, covering multiple grottoes and Cristo-from-the-sea views.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria La Bussola — wood-fired neighborhood pizzeria, pizzas from ~€8, margherita for kids
  • Za' Mariuccia — harborfront terrace since 1958, seafood — ask for plain pasta for kids
  • Taverna Rovita — Michelin-listed old-town kitchen since 1981 — ask ahead for a plain pasta for kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Arcomagno cove, Praia a Mare ↩ — a natural sea-arch cove ~25-30 min south in Calabria — swim or walk directly into it, no boat needed, and sandier than Maratea's rocky coves.
  • Diamante, Calabria ↗ — flatter mural town with a livelier promenade if Maratea’s lanes feel too steep.
  • Fiumicello Beach ↗ — easier Maratea beach day with services when sea-cave logistics feel heavy.

days.heading: Transfer: Maratea → Sorrento

facts.label: Note
facts.valueHtml: Juneteenth — observed today, confirm with your employer

days.note: If your employer observes Juneteenth on the Friday before, today's drive costs a holiday, not a PTO day. Arrive Sorrento early afternoon, settle in, an easy first evening.

days.heading: Ischia day trip

facts.label: Focus
facts.valueHtml: Sant'Angelo, Maronti Beach, optional Castello Aragonese

days.note: The direct Sorrento↔Ischia route is seasonal and has far fewer sailings than the usual island day. Confirm the 2027 timetable before locking it, and keep the island plan deliberately simple.

spots.name: Ischia
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · IschiaFlickr
spots.cost: Direct seasonal ferry from Sorrento is roughly €24-30 adult one-way, with child fare around €18; family round trip is roughly €200-240 before luggage/fees. Add island bus/taxi money or a short boat taxi if Sant'Angelo/Maronti is the focus.
spots.climate: Air ~76°F day / ~69°F night. Sea ~73°F; beaches and thermal pools make this easier than a line-based sightseeing day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Choose one side of the island: Ischia Porto/Ponte plus Castello Aragonese, or Sant'Angelo plus Maronti. Trying both ends by taxi burns money and time.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Poseidon Gardens at Citara, or a private taxi/driver between Ischia Porto and Sant'Angelo/Maronti if ferry times leave enough day.
spots.restoHtml:
• Casa Celestino — Sant'Angelo waterfront view, seafood plus simple pasta
  • Belmare Maronti Beach — casual beach restaurant and snack fallback right on Maronti
  • Pizzeria Da Gaetano — Ischia Porto/Ponte pizza fallback for a plain margherita meal
spots.altboxHtml:
• Nerano / Marina del Cantone ↩ — no-ferry beach lunch day on the Sorrento Peninsula if the Ischia timetable is awkward.
  • Minori ↗ — coastal town with an actual sandy beach and lower prices than Amalfi.
  • Maiori beach ↗ — largest easy beach on this coast if cliff-town sightseeing is not the mood.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Family-friendly Ischia ↗Sant'Angelo + Maronti guide ↗

days.heading: Amalfi, Ravello & Atrani

facts.label: Transport
facts.valueHtml: Shared boat to Amalfi, not rental car or SITA bus

facts.label: Focus
facts.valueHtml: Amalfi Duomo, Ravello's cliff-top gardens, tiny Atrani

days.note: You've already done Positano, so this day leans east — Amalfi town, the Ravello villas, and Atrani, the little fishing hamlet next door most day-trippers skip. The SS163 hairpins are a real carsickness risk, so boat in and skip the road.

spots.name: Amalfi, Ravello & Atrani
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · AmalfiIG · RavelloIG · AtraniFlickr
spots.cost: Amalfi Cathedral ~€4 adult. Villa Rufolo (Ravello) €8 adult / €6 kids 5-12. Villa Cimbrone ~€10 adult. Atrani is free to wander. Family-of-4 estimate for the two villas + Duomo: ~€60-75.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip Amalfi's paid beach club for the free public stretch, or duck one cove over to Atrani's small free beach — a quieter, gratis alternative to Amalfi's crowded, mostly-paid waterfront.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Il Flauto di Pan at Villa Cimbrone (Michelin-starred) — ~€150/person a la carte, a genuine special-occasion dinner with the Terrace of Infinity view.
spots.restoHtml:
• Le Arcate — Atrani, sea-view terrace under the arches — wood-fired pizza, margherita for kids
  • Pizzeria Donna Stella — Amalfi, lemon-garden setting, classic pizzas
  • Cumpà Cosimo — Ravello, 70+ year institution — gnocchi alla sorrentina and maccheroni al forno, a great kid option
spots.altboxHtml:
• Minori ↩ — a coastal town below Ravello with an actual sandy beach and lower prices — trades cliff-top gardens for sand.
  • Maiori beach ↗ — largest easy beach on this coast if cliff-town sightseeing is not the mood.
  • Nerano / Marina del Cantone ↗ — no-ferry beach lunch day on the Sorrento Peninsula.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Amalfi Coast with kids ↗Visiting the Amalfi Coast with kids ↗

days.heading: Procida day trip

facts.label: Focus
facts.valueHtml: Marina Corricella, Terra Murata, Chiaia or Chiaiolella beach

days.note: There is usually no convenient direct Sorrento↔Procida ferry. Use Sorrento→Naples (Beverello), then Naples→Procida (~40 min), unless a seasonal direct hydrofoil fits the 2027 schedule.

spots.name: Procida
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ProcidaFlickr
spots.cost: Naples→Procida ferries/hydrofoils usually start around €20 one-way; seasonal Sorrento direct sailings, if useful, are often ~€24-30 one-way. The island itself is free to wander.
spots.climate: Air ~80°F day / ~69°F night. Sea ~72°F — beachable, especially for a short Chiaia or Chiaiolella swim after the old town walk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk Marina Corricella and Terra Murata for free, then picnic or split lemon granita and pastries instead of a full waterfront lunch.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Small boat loop around Procida at sunset if return ferries line up — the pastel harbor looks best from the water.
spots.restoHtml:
• Bar Capriccio Procida — ferry-port stop for coffee, pastries, and a lemon granita reset
  • Caracalè — Marina Corricella waterfront restaurant for seafood with the postcard view
  • Ristorante Pizzeria Fuego — Corricella pizzeria option for a plain-margherita fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Naples historic center ↩ — gritty, lived-in, and deeply authentic if ferry timing makes Procida too awkward.
  • Nerano / Marina del Cantone ↗ — no-ferry beach lunch day on the Sorrento Peninsula.
  • Bagni Regina Giovanna ↗ — Roman ruins plus a natural swimming cove near Sorrento.

days.heading: Sorrento free day

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Marina Grande or a lemon-grove tour

days.note: One deliberately unscheduled day to decompress and repack before the flight home.

spots.name: Sorrento
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · SorrentoFlickr
spots.cost: Town is free to walk. Basic sunbed rental at Marina Grande/Piccola ~€10-12; premium beach clubs run ~€54/person. Lemon-grove/limoncello tours ~€25-55/adult.
spots.climate: Air ~76°F day / ~69°F night. Sea ~73°F — warmest water of the trip alongside Ischia and the Amalfi Coast.
spots.saveHtml: Save Basic sunbed rental at Marina Grande/Piccola (~€10-12) instead of a premium club like Peter's Beach (~€54/person) — saves ~€40+/person/day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sunset aperitivo at Vista Skybar (Hotel Mediterraneo) — 360° views over the Bay of Naples and Vesuvius, €40/person minimum spend.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria da Franco — casual wood-fired pizzeria on Corso Italia, long communal tables, margherita for kids
  • Trattoria Da Emilia — waterfront seafood trattoria since 1947, plain pasta al pomodoro for kids
  • Circolo dei Forestieri — historic 1927 terrace over the Gulf of Naples — ask ahead for a simple pasta for kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sant'Agnello ↩ — a quieter, cheaper town immediately next door — its own train station, calmer evenings, an easy walk to Sorrento's restaurants.
  • Bagni Regina Giovanna ↗ — Roman ruins plus a natural swimming cove near Sorrento.
  • Naples historic center ↗ — pizza, streets, and museums if ferry timing makes an island day awkward.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Sorrento with kids ↗What to do in Sorrento with kids ↗

days.heading: Drive to Naples, fly home
days.note: Home the evening the Pittsburgh blackout begins — don't book a tight connection today.

Getting Around

One open-jaw flight, one one-way rental car

Fly into Brindisi, drive west across the country, fly out of Naples — no backtracking, but a couple of long research caveats since 2027 fares aren't published yet.

Flights: PIT ⇄ BDS / NAP ⇄ PIT (open-jaw)

Routing1 connection each way (e.g. ITA via Rome)
Per person, open-jaw (peak June)~$1,300–1,800
Est. family (4)~$5,200–7,200
An open-jaw ticket (into Brindisi, out of Naples) prices like one round-trip, not two — earlier drafts that summed both directions overcounted. Still a current-market proxy; rebook the moment 2027 schedules open.

Rental car: one-way Brindisi → Naples

VehicleMid-size SUV recommended over 7-seat minivan
12-day rental (automatic)~$915–1,175 (minivan: $1,570–2,090)
One-way drop fee~$110–270 (estimated)
Automatics are scarce in Italy — book 3-4 months ahead. Bring an International Driving Permit from AAA; pick up/drop off at the airport locations, not city-center branches.

Ferry: Sorrento ↔ Ischia

One-way, per person~€24–30 adult / ~€18 child
Crossing~50–60 min to Ischia Porto
Est. family (4) round trip~€200–240 (~$220–265)
Direct seasonal sailings are much thinner than the usual island route — usually only a few per day in season. Check 2027 schedules before locking the day, and book the return with the outbound.

Cross-country transfers & tolls

Gallipoli → Maratea~4h23m / 290km
Maratea → Sorrento~2h28m / 200km
Sorrento → Naples Airport~1h (budget 1.5h)
Est. tolls, whole trip~€15–30
The Salerno–Reggio Calabria (A2) stretch past Maratea is toll-free; only the Naples-area A3 driving costs real tolls. Route inland via the A2, not the coastal SS106 through Calabria.

Automatics are genuinely scarce in Italy and a one-way Brindisi→Naples drop narrows inventory further. Also arrange an International Driving Permit through AAA before you leave — Italy doesn't recognize a US license alone.

Juneteenth's Friday-observance is employer-dependent

June 19, 2027 falls on a Saturday, so it's federally observed Friday June 18 — which lands on this trip's Maratea→Sorrento transfer day. That's guaranteed for federal employees but not for private employers — confirm with HR before counting on it.

There's no direct autostrada between Adriatic Puglia and Tyrrhenian Basilicata. Avoid the coastal SS106 through Calabria — it has a documented poor safety record — and route inland via the toll-free A2 instead. Build in a real rest stop.

Money & Tickets

Cash, kids, and confirmed prices

  • Book Ischia outbound and return together. The direct seasonal Sorrento route is thin; do not assume you can improvise the afternoon return.
  • Procida ferry timing matters more than tickets. Check whether the 2027 schedule gives you a direct seasonal hydrofoil or a clean Naples Beverello connection.
  • Amalfi Cathedral's ticket price is quoted as both €3 and €4 by different sources. Budget €4/adult and treat any change as a pleasant surprise.

Driving & Transfers

The one long day, done safely

  • Route Gallipoli→Maratea inland via the A2, not the coastal SS106. The Calabria stretch has a documented poor safety record — the inland autostrada is just as fast and safer.
  • Get an International Driving Permit from AAA before you leave. Italy doesn't recognize a US license alone — cheap and fast to get, but must be arranged stateside.
  • Pick up and drop off the rental car at the airport, not a city branch. Better automatic-transmission availability for a one-way Brindisi→Naples rental.
  • Budget 1.5 hours for Sorrento→Naples Airport on the fly-home day. Only 30 miles, but the Sorrentine Peninsula roads are narrow and congested near Vico Equense in summer.

Beaches & Boats

Skip lines, skip carsickness

  • Decide whether Ischia is a beach day or a thermal-park day before you go. Poseidon Gardens is a real spend; Sant'Angelo and Maronti can stay much cheaper.
  • Thermal parks have child and pool age rules. Use moderate family pools only and skip the hottest thermal pools with the 8-year-old.
  • Do the Amalfi Coast by shared boat, not rental car or SITA bus. The SS163 hairpins are a real carsickness risk — a shared boat tour (~€79-95/person) skips the road entirely.
  • The Grotta delle Meraviglie in Maratea is walk-in, not boat-only. €5/adult on foot vs €120+ for a private boat charter to see a real sea cave.

Food for Picky Eaters

A plain-pizza fallback at every base

  • Every base has a reliable margherita-pizza fallback. La Pizza da Franco (Gallipoli), Lu Tata N'zinu (Otranto), Il Graffio (Punta Prosciutto), Pizzeria da Franco (Sorrento) are all confirmed casual, kid-friendly spots.
  • Ask for pasta "in bianco" or "al pomodoro" anywhere, even nicer spots. Italian kitchens will almost always make a plain version off-menu — worth asking at Circolo dei Forestieri or Taverna Rovita rather than skipping them.
  • Da Gaetano on Ischia is the plain-pizza safety valve. Use it if the island day runs longer than planned and everyone just needs a low-friction meal.

Weather & Packing

Early-June water, midday sun

  • Sea temps run cooler in Salento/Maratea (~68-73°F) than Sorrento/Ischia/Amalfi (~72-74°F). Pack a light wetsuit top for the younger kid if they run cold — mid-June is still early season.
  • Procida is exposed between ferry waits, harbor walks, and the Terra Murata climb. Bring hats, water, and a flexible return plan in case the afternoon boat schedule shifts.
  • June is peak-pricing, not peak-crowd, season on this route. Prices run high but Salento/Maratea aren't yet at August capacity — Ischia and Amalfi will still feel busy regardless.
